title: Cognitive Biases in Cocaine Addiction: Evaluation of Interpretation Bias and its interaction with other Cognitive Biases during Inpatient Withdrawal
summary:
Everyone interprets everyday situations differently. In people with substance use disorders, so-called “cognitive distortions” are often observed. This means that ambiguous situations are unconsciously more likely to be associated with the topic of addiction. These “cognitive distortions” are also referred to as “biases.” In this study, we aim to understand what such interpretation patterns look like in cocaine addiction and how they relate to craving and attention. “Craving” means an intense, often overwhelming desire for a specific substance (e.g., nicotine, cocaine) or a behaviour (e.g., gambling). This knowledge is intended to help design future therapies with even greater precision. 

Participation in the study is completed after a single appointment.  
To investigate interpretation bias, ambiguous scenarios will be presented in text form on a computer. The task will be to complete the short texts. Additionally, we will use two computer tasks to assess cocaine-related attention and cocaine-related approach tendency. To measure attention, images of cocaine (as well as related paraphernalia) and neutral images will be presented, and participants will be asked to react to them as quickly as possible. A joystick will be used to measure the tendency to approach. Images will be presented in either portrait or landscape orientation, and participants will be asked to press left or right depending on the task.
Finally, participants will complete several questionnaires regarding their own consumption behaviour.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to use of cocaine: Dependence syndrome

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For the clinical sample:
- diagnosed cocainde dependence
- voluntary participation
- sufficient knowledge of German

For the healthy control group:
- voluntary participation
- sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
For the clinical sample:
- use of medication to aid withdrawal
- severe traumatic brain injuries
- acute psychosis
- acute suicidal tendencies
- inadequate knowledge of German
- significant cognitive impairments
- lack of legal capacity

For the healthy control group:
- use of sedative medication
- severe traumatic brain injuries
- acute psychosis
- acute suicidal ideation
- inadequate knowledge of German
- significant cognitive impairments
- lack of legal capacity
- diagnosis of a substance use disorder
